sample_unit: LLM responses (25 questions x 2 models x 3 responses)

links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and guideline concordance of LLM post-PCI discharge answers
links.effect: ChatGPT scored higher than DeepSeek in accuracy, guideline concordance, completeness, total quality (adjusted P=0.015, 0.015, 0.019, 0.005). Five-domain satisfactory rates 100.0% vs 90.7% (P=0.125).
links.quote: After pairing and Holm adjustment, ChatGPT scored higher in accuracy, guideline concordance, completeness, and total quality (adjusted P=0.015, 0.015, 0.019, and 0.005).

links.outcome: Expert-adjudicated safety flags (major error or potentially harmful recommendation) in LLM responses
links.effect: 149/150 responses (99.3%) met primary safety criterion: ChatGPT 75/75, DeepSeek 74/75 (98.7%); one DeepSeek response had major error and harmful recommendation.
links.quote: Overall, 149/150 responses (99.3%; 95% CI, 96.3%-100.0%) met the primary safety criterion: 75/75 for ChatGPT (100.0%; 95% CI, 95.2%-100.0%) and 74/75 for DeepSeek (98.7%; 95% CI, 92.8%-100.0%).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates and compares the safety and quality of responses from two LLMs (ChatGPT and DeepSeek) to standardized post-PCI patient discharge questions without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
